bull.b: Higher productivity and potentially lower manufacturing costs can improve the C1 platform’s commercial economics. If replicated at scale, this may strengthen partner adoption and support more competitive pricing across biologic production applications.

Distribution agreements, pilot sales and partner launches provide evidence that Dyadic is progressing beyond laboratory validation. Broader channel access can create recurring product, licensing and partner-derived revenue as customer qualification advances.

Exposure to several end markets reduces dependence on a single product or therapeutic program. Reusable strain-engineering and rapid protein-production capabilities may allow successful platform learnings to support broader product development.

bear.b: The current revenue base remains insufficient to absorb operating costs, leaving profitability highly dependent on future commercialization and funding events. Persistent losses can constrain investment capacity and increase dependence on external capital.

Negative equity combined with substantial cash burn weakens financial flexibility and raises refinancing or dilution risk. The company may need additional financing before operations become self-funding, potentially limiting strategic execution.

Revenue depends on customer qualification, repeat orders, grants and partner activity rather than a mature recurring base. This variability makes planning harder and may delay the scale required for durable margins and cash generation.
